answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a superlinear identity bond. Each agent locks capital to earn one vote, and the required bond grows with the square of how many identities a single controller registers. An honest agent pays one unit for one vote, but an attacker splitting into k clones pays k squared units for only k votes: ten fake agents cost a hundred times one identity while buying just ten times the influence. Caught fraud slashes every bond, so the tide of fake accounts must sit as still as marble yet can vanish like a zephyr once proof appears.
